transformations.before: Dietary fiber helps keep your child’s digestion regular and supports their heart health. It can also help them feel full longer. Choose whole grains, such as whole-grain bread, brown rice, and oatmeal. Fruits, vegetables, beans, peas, and lentils are also good sources of fiber.

transformations.before: Iron helps blood carry oxygen to your child’s muscles and other parts of their body. Iron is especially important for girls as they start menstruating (having a monthly period). Many protein foods are good sources of iron, including beef, turkey, crab, shrimp, beans, peas, and lentils. You can also get iron from dark green vegetables, such as spinach and Swiss chard, and from fortified whole- grain breakfast cereals. Pairing iron-containing foods with foods high in vitamin C, such as oranges, tomatoes, or bell peppers, can increase absorption of iron.
